title: dfilter: fix NULL deref with FT_SCALAR in compatible_ftypes
description:
## Summary

Fixes a NULL pointer dereference in `ftype_can_val_to_uinteger()` when
compiling a display filter that multiplies or divides a TIME field by
the return value of `min()` or `max()`.

## Reproduction

```
dftest -- 'frame.time > 2*min(tcp.port, udp.port)'
```

Before: SEGV (exit 134) — `FTYPE_LOOKUP` indexes `type_list[]` out of
bounds for the `FT_SCALAR` pseudo-type and dereferences NULL.

After: clean semantic error (exit 4):
`Arguments to 'min' must be of compatible type (expected Scalar, got
Unsigned integer (16 bits))`

## Root cause

`check_arithmetic_LHS_TIME()` passes `FT_SCALAR` as the logical type to
`check_function()` → `ul_semcheck_compare()` → `compatible_ftypes()`.
`compatible_ftypes()` only guarded `FT_SCALAR` as the first argument;
when received as the second argument it fell through to the integer
cases and called `ftype_can_val_to_uinteger(FT_SCALAR)`, which indexes
`type_list[FT_SCALAR]` (NULL) via `FTYPE_LOOKUP`.

A second NULL deref occurred in `ftype_pretty_name(FT_SCALAR)` when
formatting the error message.

## Changes

- `compatible_ftypes()`: handle `FT_SCALAR` explicitly via
  `FT_IS_SCALAR()` before the switch
- `ftype_name()` / `ftype_pretty_name()`: switch on the `ftenum` value
  directly instead of the `FTYPE_LOOKUP` result, so the existing
  `FT_SCALAR`/`FT_NUM_TYPES` cases become reachable
- `FTYPE_LOOKUP`: use `ws_abort_if_fail()` instead of `ws_assert()` so
  the bounds check is not compiled out in release/fuzzing builds
- 5 regression tests in `test/suite_dfilter/group_time.py`

Fixes #21377.

commits_data.message:
dfilter: fix NULL deref with FT_SCALAR in compatible_ftypes

A display filter that multiplies or divides a TIME field by the
return value of min() or max() -- e.g. `frame.time > 2*min(tcp.port,
udp.port)` -- crashed the filter compiler with a NULL pointer
dereference in ftype_can_val_to_uinteger().

check_arithmetic_LHS_TIME() passes FT_SCALAR as the logical type to
check_function(), which forwards it to compatible_ftypes() as the
second argument. compatible_ftypes() only guarded FT_SCALAR as the
first argument (via ASSERT_FTYPE_NOT_REACHED); when received as the
second argument it fell through to the integer cases and called
ftype_can_val_to_uinteger(FT_SCALAR). Since FT_SCALAR is a pseudo-type
with no entry in type_list[], FTYPE_LOOKUP indexed out of bounds and
dereferenced NULL.

A second NULL deref occurred in ftype_pretty_name(FT_SCALAR) when
formatting the type-mismatch error, because ftype_pretty_name() and
ftype_name() also called FTYPE_LOOKUP before their switch -- making
the existing FT_SCALAR/FT_NUM_TYPES cases unreachable.

Handle FT_SCALAR explicitly in compatible_ftypes() using
FT_IS_SCALAR(). Switch ftype_name() and ftype_pretty_name() to
switch on the ftenum value directly so the pseudo-type cases work.
Harden FTYPE_LOOKUP with ws_abort_if_fail() so the bounds check is
not compiled out in release builds.

Fixes #21377.
